newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA TO SELL STATE COMPANIES ON FOREIGN BOURSES.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA TO SELL STATE COMPANIES ON FOREIGN BOURSES.

text.p: Romania's main privatisation agency pressed on with plans to speed sell-offs by announcing it would privatise more than 100 state companies through stock exchanges in London, Thessaloniki and Bucharest.

"We will open a business centre in London by mid-June where we will present up to 20 companies we intend to privatise with the help of the exchange in London," State Ownership Fund (FPS) president Sorin Dimitriu said on Wednesday.

Dimitriu, speaking to reporters after a seminar on privatisation, said the companies on offer in London would be medium-sized and large enterprises. The FPS has a controlling stake in most Romanian state firms.

He said a privatisation offer for 10 to 15 small and medium companies would be launched at the exchange in the northern Greek city of Thessaloniki. Another 60 state companies would go on offer on the Bucharest stock exchange.
Dimitriu said the FPS would sell its entire stake of the companies on offer -- up to 70 percent. But he gave no indication of criteria for selecting the companies.
The FPS decided to launch Romanian selloffs on foreign exchanges because local economists say a large offer for the Bucharest bourse might trigger disruptions, Dimitriu said.
But Bucharest bourse manager Stere Farmache said such disruption was unlikely. "The market is in bad need of more liquidity. But it's a good thing the FPS thought about us."
Farmache said earlier on Wednesday that the bourse was trying to persuade the FPS to offer stakes for privatisation on its floor as a means to boost liquidity.

Leftists, who took power after the 1989 fall of communism, have been accused of stalling privatisation and restructuring moves during seven years in office ending in their election defeat last November.
The new centrist coalition government pledged to speed up selloffs. Of more than 6,500 firms slated for privatisation in 1992, some 3,100 had been sold by the end of last year.
